extracted.intended_audience: actors, improvisers, improv directors and teachers interested in scene work
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and practical instruction for creating, directing, and improving improvised scenes (two-person, group, and advanced work), including exercises and audition/advice material for performers and teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: What is improvisation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the nature of improvisation and what improvisation is.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing chapter intended to define the activity and set the ground for subsequent rules and techniques. (Page list entry only; full explanations are in the book.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of the rules of improvisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Napier 'challenges the conventional wisdom of the rules of improvisation, examining what's behind them and how they came to be in the first place.' This chapter examines rules' origins, limits, and applicability rather than treating them as absolute.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to improvise
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical techniques and approaches for performing improvisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides tangible, actionable guidance for doing scenes—intended as hands-on instruction for performers. (Catalog listing only.)

rubrics_metrics.name: "What about my partner?"
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on working with a scene partner(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers partner-related concerns such as support, listening, and relationship in a scene; addresses common partner-focused questions improvisers have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context and scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: How to establish and use context within improvised scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses the role of contextual choices in shaping a scene and how context affects choices and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and discussion of typical problems that make scenes not work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic material intended to help improvisers recognize and fix recurring scene issues. (Listed as a chapter topic.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-person scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific guidance and techniques for scenes involving two performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on dynamics and structures unique to two-person scenes, including initiation, escalation, and sustaining focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: More than two people in a scene
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice for handling group scenes with multiple performers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers roles, focus management, and keeping coherence when more than two people are onstage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of scenes involving ensemble or group improvisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overlaps with 'more than two people' but framed for ensemble work—techniques for layering, managing energy, and group dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entering scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques and considerations for entering an ongoing scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice on how to join a scene effectively so as to contribute rather than disrupt; likely includes timing, status, and offer choices. (Chapter title listed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Techniques to achieve richer, more layered scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods for adding depth and layers to improvised scenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical techniques aimed at enriching scenes beyond surface-level jokes—may include subtext, relationships, callbacks, and multi-threading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced improvisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced concepts and practices for experienced improvisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material intended to push beyond basics into more complex or risky choices, deeper scenecraft, and sophisticated ensemble play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice and guidelines for improvisers
rubrics_metrics.description: General advice and actionable guidelines aimed at improvisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A catch-all chapter offering concise, practical recommendations to bring 'strength and direction' to scenes; publisher promises 'helpful, tangible guidelines.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on audition techniques specific to improvisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice for performing in auditions—likely includes how to present skills, handle format constraints, and demonstrate scene work under pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo exercises for practice at home / Exercises to do at home
rubrics_metrics.description: Solo practice exercises improvisers can do outside of class or rehearsal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides drills and exercises for individual practice to develop skills useful in scenes; listed both as 'solo exercises for practice at home' and 'Exercises to do at home.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Improvisation and the second law of thermodynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: A conceptual/metaphorical treatment relating improvisation to entropy or similar principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An intriguingly titled chapter that likely uses metaphor to discuss scene energy, decay, and maintenance; included in contents but details are in the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annoyance
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of annoyances in improv practice or performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Likely covers pet peeves, anti-patterns, and behaviors that derail scenes or frustrate ensemble members.
